questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Rutvika's__ boldness__ in tackling new challenges was really admirable.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Timidity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"boldness"** refers to the quality of showing courage, confidence, and a willingness to take risks; it demonstrates fearlessness in handling situations. (साहस)

 
 
• **Example:** Her boldness in speaking against injustice inspired many to join the cause.
 
 
 
• **"Timidity"** refers to a lack of courage or confidence and a tendency to avoid risks or confrontations; it is the opposite of boldness. (भीरुता)
 
 
• **Example:** His timidity prevented him from voicing his opinions in the meeting.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the antonym of **'boldness'** is **'timidity'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Timidity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Confidence** (आत्मविश्वास): The feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something; firm trust.

 
 
• **Example:** She spoke with confidence during her presentation, leaving a lasting impression on the audience.
 
 
 
• **Correctness** (सही होना): The quality of being accurate or right.
 
 
• **Example:** He checked the correctness of the calculations before submitting the report.
 
 
 
• **Recklessness** (लापरवाही): Lack of care or thought about the consequences of an action.
 
 
• **Example:** His recklessness while driving led to a serious accident.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Exculpate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Condemn**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Exculpate"** means to clear someone from blame or prove that they are not guilty of wrongdoing. (दोषमुक्त करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The lawyer managed to exculpate the defendant with strong evidence proving his innocence.
 
 
 
• **"Condemn"** refers to expressing complete disapproval of someone, often in a moral or legal sense, or declaring them guilty of a crime. (निंदा करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The jury condemned the defendant for his unethical actions after reviewing all the evidence.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Exculpate' **is **'Condemn'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Condemn**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Vindicate** (सत्य साबित करना): To clear someone of blame or suspicion and prove their innocence.

 
 
• **Example:** The evidence vindicated the accused, showing that they were not involved in the crime.
 
 
 
• **Absolve** (दोषमुक्त करना): To formally declare someone free from guilt, obligation, or punishment.
 
 
• **Example:** The priest absolved him of his sins after a heartfelt confession.
 
 
 
• **Condone** (अनदेखा करना): To accept or allow morally wrong behavior to continue.
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher refused to condone cheating in the examination hall.
